title: Composition of quasi-finite ring maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Assume that both maps are of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and quasi-finite at every prime of the target in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then the composite $A\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $C$.

proof.text: Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ for $B$ as an $A$-algebra and $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ for $C$ as a $B$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. If $g:B\to C$ is the second map, the elements $g(b_1),\ldots,g(b_m),c_1,\ldots,c_n$ generate $C$ as an $A$-algebra: substitute polynomial expressions in the $b_i$ for the coefficients of a polynomial in the $c_j$. Thus the composite is of finite type, as in Stacks Tag 00F4(1), used in Tag 00PO.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PO, proof and Lemma Tag 00F4 (lemma-compose-finite-type), lines 540-594 and 30348-30349

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ and let $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p$ be its successive inverse images in $B$ and $A$. Write $\varphi:A	o B$ for the first map. For $F=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $j:B	o F$, the point $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is isolated by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Choose a basic open $D(t)=\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By the fibre-ring description in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], every element of $F$ is $j(b)/j(\varphi(a))$ with $b\in B$ and $a\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$: lift it to a fraction in the localization of $B$ at the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and then reduce modulo $\mathfrak p$. The denominator is a unit, so $D(t)=D(j(b))$. The bijection [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] and the identity $j(b)
otin\mathfrak Q\iff b
otin j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ give $b
otin\mathfrak q$, with $\mathfrak q$ the only prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$ avoiding $b$. Apply the identical argument to $B	o C$, $\mathfrak q$, and $\mathfrak r$ to obtain $c
otin\mathfrak r$ such that $\mathfrak r$ is the only prime of $C$ over $\mathfrak q$ avoiding $c$. This is the elementary translation between conditions (1) and (3) of Tag 00PK, used in Tag 00PO.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PO, proof, lines 30350-30357; Lemma Tag 00PK (lemma-isolated-point-fibre), condition (3), lines 30195-30230; Remark Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram), lines 3422-3451, for the localization/quotient description

proof.text: Write $b'=g(b)\in C$, where $g:B\to C$ is the second map. Both $b'$ and $c$ avoid $\mathfrak r$, so $b'c\notin\mathfrak r$. If a prime $\mathfrak s\subset C$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $A$ and avoids $b'c$, then $g^{-1}(\mathfrak s)$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and avoids $b$, hence equals $\mathfrak q$ by Step 2. Also $c\notin\mathfrak s$, so the other witness from Step 2 forces $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak r$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] for $A\to C$, the basic open $D(j(b'c))$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is therefore exactly $\{\overline{\mathfrak r}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus the fibre point is isolated. Step 1 supplies the finite-type hypothesis of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], proving quasi-finiteness at the arbitrary prime $\mathfrak r$ and hence the conclusion.
